PyTorch’s GRU equations imply that zero padding embeddings do not guarantee unchanged hidden states: recurrent transformations and biases still execute. Thus `padding_idx=0` alone cannot ensure padding invariance. An implementation remedy is masked recurrence: compute `h_new = GRUCell(x_t, h)`, then `h = torch.where(valid_t[:, None], h_new, h)` at every timestep and every recurrent layer. This preserves chronological updates while skipping padding. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html)

Packed sequences offer a fused alternative. Extract each history’s nonpadding tokens in chronological order, then use `pack_sequence(..., enforce_sorted=False)`, or internally right-pad those extracted histories before `pack_padded_sequence(..., batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)`. Do not pack the original left-padded tensor directly: packing retains the leading positions specified by lengths. For a unidirectional GRU, use the top-layer `h_n[-1]` as the final valid state. If `log2feats` must return aligned timestep features, unpack and scatter valid outputs back into their original left-padded positions. Handle empty histories separately. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html), [pack_sequence](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_sequence.html)

Recommended verification: in evaluation mode, compare the same history with different amounts of leading padding, alone and in mixed-length batches; check valid timestep features, final features and candidate scores within numerical tolerance. For original left-padded outputs, read the maximum nonpadding index—normally `L−1` for nonempty histories—never `count−1`. Apply identical encoding to training, diagnostics and the embedded predictor before evaluating recency interventions.
